metadata.rules_text:
- Model consistently overestimates prices in early forecast windows, especially after sharp spikes; reduce initial forecast peaks by 5–15%.
- After a significant price spike, model tends to overshoot and fail to correct downward; apply a “cool-down” factor (e.g., reduce next 3–5 days’ forecast by 2–5% from peak).
- When sentiment is neutral or absent (all 0.00), model exhibits high volatility and overconfidence; dampen forecast variance by 10–20%.
- Mean reversion is strong in 30-day horizon; if forecast is >10% above recent 7-day average, reduce by 5–10%.
- If true outcome shows sharp downward correction after a spike, model often fails to anticipate; add a “reversal buffer” to forecast 3–5 days post-spike.
- In absence of sentiment signals, model should not assume bullish momentum; default to 3–5 day moving average or 14-day SMA for baseline.
